facts.claim: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve held 282,983 thousand barrels (about 283 million) of crude oil in the week ending October 9, 2026; the last week it held less was the week ending October 15, 1982 (280,802 thousand barrels).

source.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Weekly U.S. Ending Stocks of Crude Oil in SPR (WCSSTUS1), released 10/15/2026

corroboration.name: Fox Business, 10 Aug 2026: the reserve fell below 300 million barrels, the lowest in EIA weekly data since January 1983
Rigzone, 5 Oct 2026: 283.8 million barrels in the week ending September 25, 39.69 percent of 714 million barrels of capacity (EIA data)

facts.claim: On March 11, 2026, the Department of Energy announced a 172 million barrel release from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the U.S. share of a 400 million barrel IEA collective action, in response to supply disruptions tied to the Middle East war and the Strait of Hormuz crisis.

source.name: Rigzone, USA Continues Strategic Petroleum Reserve Release, 5 Oct 2026

corroboration.name: Fox Business, 10 Aug 2026: in March 2026 President Trump authorized releasing up to 172 million barrels; Iranian attacks have disrupted tanker movement through the Strait of Hormuz
U.S. Department of Energy, United States to Release 172 Million Barrels of Oil From the Strategic Petroleum Reserve

facts.claim: During the 1973 Arab-Israeli War, Arab members of OPEC imposed an embargo against the United States; the price of oil per barrel first doubled, then quadrupled, and the embargo was lifted in March 1974.

source.name: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, Oil Embargo, 1973-1974

facts.claim: President Ford set the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in motion when he signed the Energy Policy and Conservation Act on December 22, 1975; the law made it U.S. policy to build a reserve of up to one billion barrels of petroleum.

source.name: U.S. Department of Energy, SPR Origins

corroboration.name: Bipartisan Policy Center: Congress created the reserve in the 1975 Energy Policy and Conservation Act, to buffer the economy against disruptions like the 1973 oil crisis

facts.claim: In April 1977 the government acquired several existing salt caverns on the Gulf Coast as the first storage sites, and on July 21, 1977 the first oil arrived: approximately 412,000 barrels of Saudi Arabian light crude.

source.name: U.S. Department of Energy, SPR Origins

facts.claim: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve stores its oil in naturally impermeable underground salt caverns: 61 caverns at four sites on the Gulf Coast, Bryan Mound and Big Hill in Texas and West Hackberry and Bayou Choctaw in Louisiana.

source.name: Bipartisan Policy Center, How the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve Works

corroboration.name: Congressional Research Service, The Strategic Petroleum Reserve: History, Perspectives, and Issues (RL33341): underground storage hollowed out from naturally occurring salt domes in Texas and Louisiana
